newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit higher, cash firms.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit higher, cash firms.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas were expected to open slightly higher Friday in a continuance of Thursday's rally and on early talk of firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
May over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.08 to $2.085 at 0940 EDT after settling to the upside Thursday at $2.069 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, May last traded 0.8 cent higher at $2.077 after stretching to a high of $2.09.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub. La., were talked at $2.08-2.12 per mmBtu.
Traders pegged next resistance in May at $2.095, and then at $2.12 and $2.16. May support points remained at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
"If crude goes below $19, that should kill it (May's rally)," one market source said, adding he expected some heavy selling to emerge if May nears $2.12.

In Thursday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than five cents to about $2.05. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also was quoted more than five cents higher in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Temperatures for next week are expected to run mostly below normal across the eastern half of the U.S., with warmer-than-normal weather forecast for the western third.
